title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-02-04
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality soundboard captures a mixed show with standout Hard to Handle and China Rider but a sagging Midnight Hour.
ai_review.review: The recording is a vintage sound‑board tape that suffers from hiss, distortion and occasional dropouts, yet it still conveys the energy of the night. Musically the set shines on Hard to Handle, an exploratory China Rider, and a beautifully captured Black Peter, while the Midnight Hour drags and feels bogged down. Overall the performance is solid but uneven, making it worthwhile for completists despite its technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Multiple detailed reviews describe both strong musical moments and consistent recording problems; the weighted average of show (≈3) and recording quality (≈2.5) yields a low‑mid rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hissy, garbled and occasionally distorted audio with noticeable dropouts; some sources buzz underneath and lack separation, but the tape still captures the performance.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set opens strong with Hard to Handle and moves into an exploratory China Rider, but the momentum stalls during Midnight Hour, leaving the overall flow uneven.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s vocals on Black Peter are praised as a top delivery; his solo after Midnight is described as gliding tribal funk.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh “lays it down” with Santana‑style percussion during the jam after Midnight.
